task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: effect of offensive lineup changes on shot mix
statistical power for lineup substitution studies

historical_evidence.finding: With lineup FE slope -0.0255; without lineup FE slope -0.0063; same‐shooter placebo -0.0075, indicating the apparent effect is likely due to shooter‐level confounding rather than a true lineup artifact.

Within‑unit permutation null reproduces the published suppression excess; the excess is mechanical under the selection rule and is removed by drift‑centering, pointing to selection bias and drift rather than a substantive effect.
Stacked suppression after POST_UP and PUTBACK was far smaller than additive predictions, with unexpected sign gradients and small sample sizes, and a possible implementation bug.
Penalty‑state adaptation contrasts were not distinct from adjacent‑foul placebos and standard errors were not reported, leaving the mechanism unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: selecting units on large drop and comparing to matched controls

failed_approaches.why: small sample, implementation bug, unexpected sign

evidence_establishes: Ignoring lineup fixed effects can produce an artifact in the measured effect of play types.
Selection bias and drift can generate spurious excesses in suppression analyses.
Small sample sizes and implementation bugs can undermine the reliability of stacked suppression estimates.
Placebo dependence can mask true defensive state effects.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing the offensive five actually shifts shot mix.
The magnitude or direction of personnel effects on shot distribution.
own_inferences: The research question is testable with the available data, but it requires a design that (1) includes lineup fixed effects to avoid the artifacts highlighted in [prior work][prior work], (2) controls for defensive matchup minutes and game situation to mitigate confounding, and (3) uses a sufficiently large sample of lineup changes to achieve adequate power.
uncertainties: Exact frequency of lineup changes across the four seasons and whether that provides enough data to detect modest shifts in shot mix.
Reliability and granularity of shot‑type categorization in the derived possession records.
Potential unobserved confounders that correlate with both lineup changes and shot decision (e.g., injury, coaching strategy).

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved evidence highlights methodological pitfalls but does not provide a definitive answer to the personnel‑shot‑mix question; it informs the design rather than altering the decision to proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup changes may be driven by game‑state or injury factors that also influence shot selection.
Lineup changes are relatively infrequent, potentially limiting sample size.
Shot mix categories may be noisy or misclassified across play‑by‑play data.
Players and lineups may be selected for substitution based on expected performance, creating reverse causality.
Placebo contrasts may be correlated with the treatment, masking true effects.

prior_work.summary: Prior studies have documented artifacts arising from omitted lineup fixed effects, selection bias, drift, and small samples in related basketball analytics questions, but none have directly quantified the effect of an offensive lineup change on shot mix.

risks.text: Lineup changes may be triggered by game context (e.g., score margin, fatigue) that also influences shot selection.
Limited number of lineup changes reduces statistical power.
Shot‐type labels derived from play‑by‑play may contain errors or inconsistencies.
Substitutions are made to improve performance, potentially creating reverse causality.
Placebo contrasts may be correlated with the treatment, obscuring effects.

design.estimand: Effect of an offensive lineup change on the probability distribution of shot types (e.g., 0–3 ft, 3–15 ft, 15–23 ft, 23–30 ft, 30‑plus) conditioned on defensive matchup and game state.
design.unit: Individual possession following a substitution event.
design.sample: All possessions in which the offensive lineup changes (substitution in or out of the five) across the 2022‑23 to 2024‑25 seasons, matched to comparable control possessions in the same game and period without a lineup change.
design.power: Target 80% power to detect a 5‑percentage‑point shift in any shot‑type probability, assuming a baseline shot‑type probability of ~20% and an effective sample size of ~10,000 lineup‑change possessions.
design.controls: Lineup fixed effects, defensive matchup minutes (or player‑by‑player matchup exposure), team and opponent fixed effects, game‑state covariates (score margin, period, time remaining), and period‑specific intercepts.
design.falsification: Test the same lineup‑change estimate on defensive lineup changes (which should not affect offensive shot mix) and on a placebo window (e.g., a 2‑minute window before the actual substitution).
design.multiplicity: Apply Holm‑Bonferroni correction across the five shot‑type categories; report both unadjusted and adjusted p‑values.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null hypothesis of no shot‑mix shift if the adjusted p‑value < 0.05 for any shot‑type category. Provide confidence intervals for the estimated changes.
design.data_version: NBA 2022‑23 to 2024‑25 per‑game play‑by‑play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, and derived possession records as of 2026‑11‑02.
